notes: Flat 3.5% for tax year 2026 (HB 1 of 2025; DOR withholding page). 2026 standard deduction $3,360 (DOR announcement, KRS 141.081); 2027 will be $3,470.

Kentucky has no head-of-household status. On a joint return only one standard deduction is allowed (Form 740/740-NP instructions); spouses may instead file separately on a combined return, each claiming a deduction against their own income (not modeled; it only helps when both spouses have income).

Not modeled: family size tax credit (low income), personal tax credits for age 65+/blind, itemized deductions, Kentucky adjustments to federal AGI (e.g., pension exclusion), and the LLET credit for single-member LLC owners.
Local occupational license taxes (see localIncomeTax) are not modeled.
Kentucky uses the Internal Revenue Code as of December 31, 2024 (static conformity, DOR Individual Income Tax page); the SE-tax, SE health insurance and SEP/solo 401(k) adjustments are unaffected.

seDeduction.note: Inherited: Kentucky AGI starts from federal AGI.

retirementContributions.note: SEP-IRA and solo 401(k) deductions are inherited through federal AGI.

qbi.note: The federal QBI deduction is below AGI and is not part of Kentucky taxable income.

localIncomeTax.note: Many Kentucky cities, counties and some school districts levy occupational license taxes on wages and on self-employment net profits (rates and bases vary widely). They are administered locally, not by DOR, and are not universal, so they are not modeled; check your city/county occupational license office.

localities.name: Lexington-Fayette
localities.note: Lexington-Fayette Urban County Government charges a 2.25% occupational license fee on compensation and on business net profits. Any separate school district tax is not included.

sources.title: Occupational license fee: rates and current forms - City of Lexington, Kentucky

estimatedTax.threshold: Estimated payments may be required if you expect more than $5,000 of income not subject to Kentucky withholding; no payment is required if the year's estimated tax is $500 or less.
estimatedTax.safeHarbor: Underpayment penalty avoided if payments equal 90% of current-year tax or 100% of prior-year tax (110% if prior-year Kentucky AGI exceeded $150,000; $75,000 MFS); no penalty if the shortfall is $500 or less (Form 2210-K).

businessCosts.annualReportFee: $15 annual report, due by June 30 each year after formation.
businessCosts.franchiseOrMinimumTax: Limited Liability Entity Tax (LLET): a single-member LLC owned by an individual must file Form 725 and pays at least the $175 minimum; owner gets a nonrefundable credit for LLET above $175 against income tax on the LLC's income. Sole proprietors are not subject to LLET.
businessCosts.grossReceiptsTax: LLET is measured on gross receipts/gross profits, but businesses with total gross receipts or gross profits of $3 million or less pay only the $175 minimum (sliding scale $3M-$6M; 0.095% of gross receipts or 0.75% of gross profits above $6M).
